report:
### Conclusion
**No.** High-quality scientific evidence demonstrates that saw palmetto (*Serenoa repens*) preparations do not improve lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) compared to placebo in the longer term.

### Evidence
Rigorous double-blind clinical trials and systematic reviews consistently indicate that saw palmetto performs no better than placebo:

1. **2006 NEJM Trial:** A landmark one-year, double-blind randomized controlled trial evaluated standard daily saw palmetto extract (320 mg) and found no statistically significant difference compared to placebo in urinary symptom scores, peak urinary flow rate, or prostate size (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa053085).
2. **2011 CAMUS Trial (*JAMA*):** A multi-center trial evaluated escalating doses of saw palmetto extract up to 960 mg/day (triple the standard dose) over 72 weeks. High-dose saw palmetto did not reduce BPH symptoms or improve urinary flow compared to placebo (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/1104439).
3. **Cochrane Systematic Reviews:** Synthesizing data across 27 randomized controlled trials, Cochrane reviews concluded with high certainty that *Serenoa repens* provides little to no meaningful benefit for BPH-related urinary symptoms, flow rates, or quality of life over short- or long-term durations (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD001423_serenoa-repens-benign-prostatic-hyperplasia).
4. **NIH NCCIH Assessment:** The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health confirms that large-scale rigorous trials demonstrate saw palmetto is not superior to placebo for managing BPH symptoms (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/providers/digest/spotlight-on-saw-palmetto-science).
